facts.text: Indigenous people occupied the peninsula at the convergence of the Umatilla and Columbia rivers for at least ten thousand years.
The Lewis and Clark Expedition noted a village on the site of Umatilla in their journals during their 1806 return trip.
Umatilla was once a vital commercial center because rapids on the Columbia River forced boats to transfer cargo or portage.
The original townsite of Umatilla was abandoned after the United States Corps of Engineers determined it would be flooded by a dam.
Umatilla contains the largest existing prehistoric site reported in the state of Oregon, where thousands of ancient relics were found.
The original street grid of Umatilla is still visible north of the railroad tracks as a nature preserve and archaeological site.
